properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured on 0.79.0): reflow2's update path has no step before the binary is replaced. UPDATING.md says replacing the binary is the whole procedure, and its rollback advice needs a backup it never asks for. install.sh overwrites the binary and keeps nothing. The new binary's first open then repairs and restamps the store, and on every one-shot door it says nothing. So a backup taken after the install is not a pre-upgrade backup, and nothing shows that it is not
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-10-05, triaging art:vscode-call-field-log-2026-10-05: entry [friction] (lines 345-349), and the rollback half of entry [friction] (lines 362-365).

① OBSERVED, the reporter's words: "the recipe's order (export, then back up, before upgrading) could not be followed: the new binary was installed (11:55) before the recipe was run (11:59), so every 'pre-upgrade' export and backup was taken by 0.79.0, which may already have repaired the store on open." And the rollback step `cp ~/.local/bin/reflow2-mcp ~/.local/bin/reflow2-mcp.0.76.0` "hard-codes the old version. Run after the install (as here) it would save a 0.79.0 binary under a 0.76.0 name." EXPECTED: a rollback point exists before anything is replaced. NOT AFFECTED: the stores themselves. 0.79.0 opens a 0.76.0 store, additive only.

② PRECEDENT: dec:backup-belongs-to-the-consumer (accepted 2026-08-06). reflow2 does not back a design up. It owes "a documented update path and honest primitives", and its part (3) is "not lying when something is off". Also fact:root-cause-an-upgrade-under-a-session-is-known-at-open-and-said-only-to-stderr-2026-09-28. Nothing recorded is about the ORDER of an upgrade.

③ CANDIDATES:
(A) the recipe's order, which came from the maintainer's agent in chat and is not reflow2's (fact:the-0-79-0-install-near-miss-came-from-a-recipe-written-in-chat-not-from-reflow2-2026-10-05).
(B) reflow2's documented path has no step before the install.
(C) the installer keeps no rollback copy.
(D) the new binary changes the store on its first open, so a later backup differs from the pre-upgrade state.
(E) the observation is wrong, and the open does not change the store.

④⑤ MEASURED:
- (B) HOLDS. getting-started/UPDATING.md, "Updating a locally-installed reflow2", says: "Replace the binary. That is the whole procedure", then gives the install.sh one-liner. Its only rollback advice is "restore the store from a backup taken before the upgrade, or re-`--import` a committed export from that era". No step asks for that backup, or says when to take it. "Backups are yours" describes hosted deployments only.
- (C) HOLDS. tools/install.sh runs `install -m 755 "$tmp/reflow2-mcp" "$BIN_DIR/reflow2-mcp"` over the old binary, keeps no copy, and ends "Your design graphs are never touched." install.sh is not registered as an Artifact, so the design is silent about it.
- (D) HOLDS, and (E) is REFUTED. A store was written by 0.74.0 with a Flow carrying `entry_point` and a Capability carrying `is_entry_point`. Then `reflow2-mcp --export` was run with 0.79.0. The export lacks both values, graph.meta.json now says 0.79.0, and stderr has only the INFO "opening" line. The next loop_status has no `repaired_on_open`. `reflow2 read graph_report` does the same. So an "export before upgrading", run after the install, is a post-upgrade export, and nothing marks it as one (fact:root-cause-every-one-shot-open-drops-the-version-verdict-and-the-repair-report-2026-10-05).
- (A) HOLDS for the near-miss, and is not the class. The binary was replaced at 11:55, so no recipe given at 11:59 could have produced a pre-upgrade backup.

⑥ CLASS: an upgrade is a one-way step, and its rollback point has to be taken before it. reflow2's documented path starts at the replacement. The accepted boundary settles who keeps backups. It never said WHEN a person should take one, and that belongs to part (1), the documented update path the decision says reflow2 owes. Would a fix here have stopped the field case? A "before you install" step in UPDATING.md would have. So would an installer that kept the replaced binary under its version name.

SIDE MEASUREMENT. UPDATING.md says "Downgrading is NOT currently checked ... no verdict and no warning today". On the stdio server that has been wrong since 2026-09-15: 0.78.0 serving a 0.79.0-stamped store prints "BEHIND it" and serves served_by.behind_record. Through `--call` it is still true: no warning, no behind_record, and the stamp is rewritten down to 0.78.0.

⑦⑧ NOTHING BUILT. Idea: dec:idea-installing-over-an-older-reflow2-leaves-a-rollback-point-first.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: what the field machine's 0.76.0 stores held that 0.79.0 repaired. The log names only retired Flow and Capability values on one member. How the binary came to be installed at 11:55, before the recipe, is not in the log.
